description: Field names that MUST NOT appear on the current Cokret v1 wire in the contexts listed below. Each entry pins the context (top-level envelope, specific payload class, etc.) because a name may be legal elsewhere. cotest scanner walks Event Envelope / payload bytes and flags any occurrence outside the entry's allowed_contexts.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: Reducer / parser MUST fail with schema_violation when the field appears in the listed context.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Readers MAY tolerate the field during a bounded migration window but writers MUST NOT emit it.
rejection_levels.compat_only: Allowed only on explicit interop / compatibility surfaces.
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from machine surfaces; survives in CHANGELOG / migration notes.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: Reference in CHANGELOG or migration documentation.
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: Reference in time-bounded migration code that rewrites stored legacy bytes.
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: Reference in an explicit interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the field.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: Reference in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert rejection.

entries.notes: Legacy Matrix-style 'branch' top-level field on timeline / Flow events is replaced by the v1 'track' concept (a display-only timeline segment identifier). See current-model 'Track 是纯展示 / 时间线分段标识'. The string 'branch' MUST NOT appear as a top-level Event Envelope or payload field name.
Wire fields that carry one concrete Flow.tracks map key use `track_name`. The plural `tracks` map and `allowed_tracks` capability constraint remain valid collection names.

When the plaintext counterpart is `content`, the encrypted counterpart is `encrypted_content` (Flow, Message, Morph). Generic `encrypted_payload` remains valid for non-content carriers such as identity and reaction payloads.

Flow and Morph user-readable title is metadata. It MUST NOT be a top-level object wire field; in MLS / E2EE scopes it travels inside encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

Flow and Morph user-readable summary is metadata. It MUST NOT be a top-level object wire field; in MLS / E2EE scopes it travels inside encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.
Extensible user metadata fields live under metadata.fields, or inside encrypted_metadata when the effective metadata profile requires encryption.
Room core model was removed; Realm is the v1 boundary. 'room_kind' MUST NOT appear on the wire outside an explicit MIMI / Matrix interop module.

Flow payload field 'kind' (or any analogous discriminator) MUST NOT carry the literal value 'room'. Use 'realm' / 'flow' / canonical Realm.kind values. Interop translation lives in an opt-in interop module only.

Flow payload MUST NOT carry 'discussion_space_ref'. Discussion privacy is represented by Circle-scoped Flow objects and confidential_discussion_of Relation facts; the field-level Circle identifier is 'scope_circle_id' (see schemas/flow.schema.json, zh/models/circle.md).

entries.replacement: parent_space_id / default_realm_id / scope_circle_id / default_scope_circle_id / retention_policy_id / disclosure_policy_id / rate_limit_policy_id / policy_id
entries.notes: Single concrete protocol object identifiers use `_id`; `_ref` is reserved for causal, proof, schema/profile, content-addressed, or polymorphic reference material. The old fields parent_ref, default_realm_ref, scope_ref, default_scope_ref, retention_policy_ref, disclosure_policy_ref, rate_limit_policy_ref, and Policy-object policy_ref MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

entries.replacement: allowed_view_ids / allowed_flow_ids / allowed_circle_ids / denied_flow_ids / allowed_space_ids / denied_space_ids / realm_ids / approval_actor_ids
entries.notes: Capability grant constraints that contain one concrete identifier kind use `_ids`, not `_refs`. The old fields allowed_view_refs, allowed_flow_refs, allowed_circle_refs, denied_flow_refs, allowed_space_refs, denied_space_refs, realm_refs, and approval_actor_refs MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire. Polymorphic container constraints allowed_from_container_refs / allowed_to_container_refs remain `_refs` because they may identify Space, Flow, or Morph containers.
The abbreviated media participant typed ID prefix was expanded to the full snake_case kind. Current v1 wire MUST use ck:rtc_participant:<uuid>; ck:rtcpart:<uuid> is rejected.
Key backup KDF params use digest_algorithm for PBKDF2/derived digest selection. The old params.hash selector is ambiguous with digest bytes and MUST NOT appear on current v1 wire.

member_delivery_binding references the policy revision Event that authorized a delivery binding, not a Policy object. The field therefore carries explicit event-reference semantics as policy_event_ref.
The child_scope_policy discriminator now names the concrete field it requires: scope_circle_id.

Range-completeness event_range, audit RYW receipt, and POST /events response MUST use 'realm_frontier'. The replication and security boundary covered by this frontier is the Realm, not an in-Realm Space container. 'space_frontier' MUST NOT appear on the current wire as a frontier object property.

Relation MUST carry rank at the top level, not nested under fields. The dual-source (top-level rank vs fields.rank) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level rank only, and readers MUST reject fields.rank with schema_violation. See zh/models/relation.md §2.
Space MUST carry rank at the top level. Mirrors the relation_payload constraint; closes the dual-source ambiguity uniformly. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md §3.2.

Space is a container, not a security boundary. A legacy space-create / space-update payload carrying Realm-level security_class is the pre-inversion Space-as-boundary shape and MUST be rejected; migrate it to Realm payload fields.

entries.replacement: ck.realm.join_rule or ck.realm.policy_components join policy facet
entries.notes: Join policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry join_rule; this closes the current Space container model versus removed pre-inversion payload-shape ambiguity.
History visibility is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry history_visibility.
Policy server attachment is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry policy_server.
Delivery binding policy is Realm-scoped. Space payloads MUST NOT carry delivery_binding_policy.

ck.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. The reducer initializes revision_root to the new message_id; only ck.message.revise (and subsequent revise events) may set revision_root, and only to the create's revision_root. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §9.

Composite Content Block MUST use the field name `parts` (matching schemas/message.schema.json, schemas/event-payload.schema.json, schemas/flow.schema.json, and schemas/morph.schema.json). The temporary `blocks` spelling was rejected because it over-constrained the concept to document layout blocks; the canonical wire name is `parts`, and `blocks` MUST NOT appear in current content_block_composite wire. See zh/models/content-types.md §4.10.

Encrypted Envelope MUST NOT carry `cleartext_commitment`. The bare plaintext hash is dictionary-attackable offline against low-entropy plaintext; v1 E2EE producers MUST NOT emit it and receivers MUST reject any envelope that carries it (top-level `not.required` in schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json). Future profiles needing plaintext commitment MUST define a keyed/salted form rather than this bare hash.

Flow MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). The dual-source (top-level stage vs metadata.fields.stage) ambiguity is closed: writers MUST emit top-level stage only, and readers MUST reject metadata.fields.stage with schema_violation. Same constraint as fields.rank in relation_payload / space_payload. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 and zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.

Flow stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level. It MUST NOT be smuggled under metadata.fields.* and MUST NOT be supplied by actor on wire (reducer overwrites with the triggering ck.flow.stage.set event's created_at). See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 rule 3.

entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard. Flow stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note / explanation field anywhere — neither on the object, nor in the ck.flow.stage.set payload, nor under metadata.fields.*. Human-readable rationale belongs in a Message on the Flow's discussion track that 'references' the stage event; audit attribution is provided by the event log's own actor_id / created_at. The metadata.fields.stage_reason path MUST be rejected to prevent implementations from re-introducing the field through a back door.

entries.replacement: Message on the Flow's discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for metadata.fields.stage_reason. Closes 'stage_note' / 'stage_comment' / 'stage_explanation' style re-spellings via metadata.fields.*. Same canonical channel: a Message on the discussion track that references the ck.flow.stage.set event.

entries.replacement: stage (top-level Flow field) or state (physical lifecycle)
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard: 'lifecycle' is reserved terminology for the state axis (archive / restore / tombstone lifecycle events). It MUST NOT appear on the wire as a metadata.fields.* key on Flow. Business-progression goes through the top-level 'stage' field; physical lifecycle through 'state'. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.

Reserved-name guard: 'progress_state' is a sister name for the stage concept and MUST NOT appear under metadata.fields.*. Implementations expressing business progression MUST use the canonical top-level 'stage' field.

Reserved-name guard: 'status' is the most direct sister spelling of the stage concept and MUST NOT appear as a metadata.fields.* key on Flow. Business progression goes through the canonical top-level 'stage' field; physical lifecycle through 'state'. Domain data mirrored from external systems MUST use a domain-named key (e.g. fields.jira_status), not bare 'status'.

Flow assignment is single-sourced by the standard assigned_to Relation. metadata.fields.assignee would create a second truth source and MUST be rejected; UI labels may say Assignee but wire writes create/tombstone assigned_to Relation edges.
Plural spelling of the Flow assignment field alias is forbidden for the same reason as metadata.fields.assignee. Multiple assignees are represented by multiple active assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is already the standard Relation kind and MUST NOT be reused as a Flow metadata field.

entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations
entries.notes: assigned_actor_ids is a derived projection field, not Flow object state. Writers MUST NOT persist it under metadata.fields.
Morph MUST carry stage at the top level (required field). Mirror of the flow_payload fields.stage constraint.
Morph stage_changed_at is reducer-derived and lives at the top level.

entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the ck.morph.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph. Stage transitions carry no reason field; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message that references the ck.morph.stage.set event.

entries.replacement: Message on an associated discussion track that references the ck.morph.stage.set event
entries.notes: Reserved-name sister-guard for Morph fields.stage_reason. Same forbidden surface as Flow.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph: 'lifecycle' is reserved for the state axis.
Reserved-name guard mirror for Morph.

ck.flow.update payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only ck.flow.stage.set may mutate these fields. The wire-level guard is the same pattern as forbidding ck.message.create from carrying revision_root — a forbidden patch path on an otherwise-shared payload class. cotest scanners MUST flag any patch op whose path matches /^stage(_changed_at)?$/. See zh/models/flow-and-message.md §3.2 reducer hard constraint 5.
ck.flow.update MUST NOT patch assignment through Flow metadata. Assignment writes create or tombstone assigned_to Relation edges.
Plural assignment metadata patch alias is forbidden; multiple assignees are multiple assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is a Relation kind, not a Flow metadata patch path.

entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations
entries.notes: assigned_actor_ids is projection-only and MUST NOT be written through ck.flow.update.
Legacy Flow fields.* patch paths are not the canonical metadata path; assignment is Relation-sourced regardless of spelling.
Legacy plural assignment patch alias is forbidden; multiple assignees are multiple assigned_to Relation edges.
assigned_to is a Relation kind, not a Flow metadata patch path.

entries.replacement: read-only projection assigned_actor_ids derived from assigned_to Relations
entries.notes: assigned_actor_ids is projection-only and MUST NOT be written through legacy fields.* patch paths.

ck.morph.update / ck.morph.schema_migrate payload's patch MUST NOT include path 'stage' or 'stage_changed_at'. Stage transitions are single-source: only ck.morph.stage.set may mutate these fields. See zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3.3 reducer hard constraint 6 and zh/models/morph.md §2.

Validity upper bounds use expires_at. Current writers MUST NOT emit not_after.

Event proofs MUST bind canonical Event bytes with event_digest. Generic non-Event detached proofs now use payload_digest. payload_hash is forbidden in all wire contexts.

Generic detached-JWS proofs over non-Event canonical payloads (Seal signature, identity-link, did-continuity, erasure receipts, etc.) MUST use payload_digest. This aligns with the v1 hash-vocabulary rule (common-fields.md §2): output bytes use <noun>_digest; algorithm selector uses <noun>_algorithm; tree roots use <noun>_root. _hash is forbidden as a wire field-name suffix.

Policy check chain bare `actor` renamed to actor_id (did_id_suffix rule). Applies to PolicyCheckRequestBody.actor, PolicyCheckOutcome bound_to.actor, challenge obligation bound_to.actor and capability vector request.actor. Registered under the dotted bound_to.actor path because the bare token `actor` remains a legitimate enum value (resource selector kind, target.kind) and prose noun — literal scanners MUST NOT flag every `actor` token.

MIMI consent update request body bare `actor` renamed to actor_id (did_id_suffix rule: protocol responsibility subjects use the _id suffix even when the value is a DID). Scoped to the mimi_update_consent_request_body context (mimi-operations.schema.json); the bare token `actor` remains a legitimate enum value and prose noun elsewhere — literal scanners MUST NOT flag every `actor` token.

MIMI consent request body bare `requester` renamed to requester_id (did_id_suffix rule: protocol responsibility subjects use the _id suffix even when the value is a DID). Scoped to the mimi_request_consent_request_body context (mimi-operations.schema.json); `requester` remains in use on other interop request bodies (key material, identifier query, proxy download) and as a prose noun — literal scanners MUST NOT flag every `requester` token.

ServiceDescribe.verified_profiles entry field cotest_run_id renamed to verification_run_id (conformance_verifier_neutralization): the wire contract binds to the neutral Conformance Verifier role (conformance-suite.md §6.2), not to a specific downstream tool name. cotest remains a legitimate informative prose name for the reference verifier implementation — literal scanners MUST NOT flag prose mentions of cotest.

ServiceDescribe.verified_profiles entry field cotest_issuer_did renamed to verifier_did (conformance_verifier_neutralization): the signing authority is the neutral Conformance Verifier role (conformance-suite.md §6.2), not a specific downstream tool name. The companion claim_kind enum value rename cotest_verified → conformance_verified is registered in renames.json (cotest_verified#service_describe_claim_kind).
Directory / projection rows use canonical title, not a name alias.
Directory / projection rows use canonical avatar_blob_ref, not an avatar alias.
Directory / projection rows use canonical owning_organizations, not an official_organizations alias.

Push-notification payload MUST NOT carry the pre-inversion 'space_name' field. After the Realm/Space inversion the human-readable label that a push gateway might surface comes from either the Realm (realm_title) or plaintext-visible Flow metadata.title (flow_title); both remain forbidden in the ck.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 baseline (privacy default) and are only permitted under the explicit ck.profile.push_gateway.visible_notification.v1 opt-in profile. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §3 and fixtures/privacy-security-fixture.json forbidden_fields_absent.
Moderation visibility enum values use the full franking_proof noun.
Moderation evidence policy fields use the full franking_proof noun.
Retention time upper bounds use the canonical expires_at suffix.
Moderation queue item's own typed identifier uses the common id field.
Account subscribe to_device container carries DeviceMessageEnvelope objects, not Event envelopes.
Realm freeze time upper bounds use the canonical expires_at suffix with a domain prefix.
Agent audit binding subject is a protocol actor DID-as-id.
Snapshot chunk descriptors use digest with an algorithm prefix.
Handle claim delivery binding evidence is single-sourced inside member_delivery_binding.
Handle claim delivery binding policy references are single-sourced inside member_delivery_binding.

Generic object_patch_payload single-sources the target object via 'target_ref'. The pre-2026-05-24 draft also accepted 'object_ref' and even target-less patches; both shapes are removed. This forbids only the payload property name; event-payload.schema.json $defs.object_ref and selector grammar object_ref remain valid generic reference terms.

Generic object_lifecycle_payload single-sources the target object via 'target_ref'. The pre-2026-05-24 draft also accepted 'object_ref' or even a target-less {target_state} form; both shapes are removed. This forbids only the payload property name; event-payload.schema.json $defs.object_ref and selector grammar object_ref remain valid generic reference terms.
Federation verification payloads use the v1 hash vocabulary: digest fields end in _digest and values use <algo>:<lowercase_hex>.
MemberIdentity display_profile reuses the canonical avatar_blob_ref name for Blob references.
Applet protocol metadata exposes a Blob reference, so the field carries the _blob_ref suffix.
Media visibility is aligned with Realm / Circle scope; Space is not a security boundary.
Blob metadata uses content_digest with an algorithm prefix. Content-addressed blob_ref values may still use ck:blob:sha256:<hex>.
Blob upload request and response byte counts use size_bytes; bare size is not a byte-count field name in v1.
Custom signature algorithm selector fields use the full _algorithm suffix.
Custom device key algorithm selector fields use the full _algorithm suffix.
Agent key payloads name the agent as a protocol responsibility principal, not raw DID ecosystem material.
Audit release evidence names the attested release actor with _id; service_did remains the hosting service DID.
Accountability in agent key payloads points at a DID-as-principal and therefore uses _id.
Blob metadata thumbnail references use _blob_ref.
Agent lifecycle payloads mutate the status axis; the transition timestamp must name that axis.
Handle Claim's closed protocol discriminator uses claim_kind. claim_type remains valid in external credential selector contexts.
Seal signatures use the full signature noun.
DID continuity evidence uses public_key rather than pubkey.
Recovery share commitments use base64url characters and therefore carry _b64u.

entries.replacement: actor_kind=integration or actor_kind=agent plus Applet provenance
entries.notes: Ghost Actor is not a wire actor_kind enum value. External account mirrors should use integration; Applet-managed AI / automation actors may use agent.

entries.replacement: actor_kind=agent plus native agent provisioning state
entries.notes: Native personal agent is represented by actor_kind=agent and CKP-0008 provisioning/accountability state, not by an expanded actor_kind enum.

entries.replacement: actor_kind=integration or actor_kind=agent plus Applet provenance
entries.notes: Ghost/native distinction is carried by Applet provenance and accountability, not by an expanded actor_kind enum.

entries.replacement: owning user/org principal DID as actor_id; device identity via device_id (ck:device:<uuid>) + ck.device.authorize
entries.notes: A device is not an actor principal and has no DID of its own. Device actions are attributed to the owning principal DID; the device is identified by device_id and registered as a verification method under that principal DID. See zh/models/actor.md and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md.

Actor Profile accountability targets are a list of responsibility-subject principal DIDs; the field uses the _ids suffix (plural of the scalar accountable_principal_id). The _to preposition suffix is outside the _id/_ref/_did taxonomy and is removed.
The {threshold, of} reviewer quorum object names the DID list reviewers (mirrors approvers / recovery_members). The two-letter of is not a valid wire field name.
The membership delivery routing list carries service DIDs; the field names the value category explicitly as via_service_dids. Bare via is removed.
Each signature-chain link names the signing principal as principal_id (DID-as-id responsibility subject); the signing key remains verification_method. The two-letter by is removed.

Human-readable policy duration wire values use ISO 8601 (PT24H, P30D, P1Y). The self-invented compact form ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h|d)$ (e.g. 24h, 7d, 15m) MUST NOT appear on the wire; see common-fields.md §3.0.2 and constraint-schema.md §3. Machine timing fields continue to use integer _ms / _seconds.
